questions.q: What did Mattis find at the officer training program in Quantico?
a: A sense of purpose
A college degree
A publishing contract
A medical discharge
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Mattis as directionless until Quantico gave him a calling he refused to leave.

questions.q: Which three qualities does Mattis name as the marks of an effective leader?
a: Competence, care, and conviction
Courage, charisma, and cunning
Discipline, loyalty, and humility
Vision, strategy, and speed
questions.why: Lesson 2 builds its leadership advice around being skilled, showing you care and holding firm rules.

questions.q: What does Mattis compare a military leader to when describing care?
a: A coach who pushes subordinates to grow
A friend who shares their troubles
A parent who shields them from risk
A judge who settles their disputes
questions.why: Lesson 2 says leaders cannot be friends with subordinates and should act more like a coach developing their strengths.

questions.q: Why does Mattis say the US struggled after Saddam Hussein fell?
a: It failed to plan for the chaos that followed
It sent too few troops to win the war
It relied on allies who soon withdrew
It underestimated Iraq's oil reserves
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that a lack of preparation left the US unprepared for the disorder after the regime collapsed.

questions.q: What specific problem did Iraq's defeated army create?
a: Trained young men with no jobs or prospects
A shortage of weapons for US troops
A flood of refugees into Europe
A collapse in global oil prices
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls the unemployed, battle-hardened soldiers a disaster waiting to happen that could be turned against US forces.
